title: Rocky Mountain Summer in Alberta: 5 days of turquoise lakes, glacier hikes & Canada Day magic for two
description: Alberta in July is pure Rocky Mountain magic — impossibly blue glacial lakes, wildflower meadows in full bloom, and long golden evenings that stretch past 10pm. This itinerary takes you from Calgary's Canada Day buzz up through Banff's iconic peaks, along the legendary Icefields Parkway to Jasper, and back through some of the most jaw-dropping landscapes on Earth. Two people, five days, zero regrets.

days.title: Canada Day in Calgary
days.description: Fly into Calgary on Canada's birthday and dive into the celebrations. Stephen Avenue pedestrian mall comes alive with live music, street performers, and red-and-white crowds. The evening fireworks over the Bow River are stunning.

activities.name: Canada Day on Stephen Avenue
activities.description: Calgary's main pedestrian strip becomes a massive outdoor party on July 1. Live stages, food vendors, street performers, and thousands of people waving maple leaf flags. A perfect way to feel the Canadian pride energy. Escape the main crowds with a stroll along the Bow River pathway. The Eau Claire area has beautiful green spaces and river views — ideal for a Canada Day picnic.

activities.name: Canada Day Fireworks over Calgary
activities.description: Head to Prince's Island Park or the Bow River pathway for the best fireworks views. The show typically starts at 11pm when it finally gets dark in July — Calgary's northern latitude means incredibly long summer days.

days.neighborhoods: Banff Town · Vermilion Lakes · Lake Minnewanka
days.title: Banff — Into the Rockies
days.description: Drive the Trans-Canada Highway west from Calgary and enter Banff National Park — the moment the peaks come into view, you'll understand why people travel across the world for this. Explore the charming town of Banff, paddle on Vermilion Lakes, and cruise the vast Lake Minnewanka as the alpenglow paints the mountains pink.

activities.name: Drive Calgary to Banff (90 minutes)
activities.description: The Trans-Canada Highway west from Calgary is one of the world's great drives — mountains grow on the horizon until they're towering all around you. Stop at the Banff National Park gate for your first Rocky Mountain selfie. Just minutes from downtown Banff, the three Vermilion Lakes mirror Mount Rundle in still water. Rent a canoe or kayak from the Banff Canoe Club and paddle through this wildlife-rich wetland — great blue herons, elk, and beavers are common sightings.

activities.name: Lake Minnewanka Boat Cruise
activities.description: Hop on a Pursuit boat cruise on Lake Minnewanka — at 21km long, it's one of the largest lakes in the Canadian Rockies. Mountain peaks tower on every side, and your guide shares the story of the ghost town that was flooded to make this reservoir. Browse Banff's charming main street — a mix of outfitter shops, galleries, fudge shops, and mountain-chic boutiques. Pop into the Banff Park Museum (Canada's oldest natural history museum) for a quick wildlife education.

days.neighborhoods: Lake Louise · Moraine Lake · Icefields Parkway North
days.title: Lake Louise & Moraine Lake — Turquoise Perfection
days.description: Today is perhaps the most visually spectacular day you'll have anywhere on Earth. The glacially-fed waters of Lake Louise and Moraine Lake glow an impossible turquoise-blue, surrounded by sheer mountain walls dusted with snow. Start before dawn — the early light and calm water are otherworldly.

activities.name: Moraine Lake at Sunrise
activities.description: The Valley of the Ten Peaks reflected in Moraine Lake's brilliant blue water is Canada's most iconic image — and seeing it at sunrise with mist rising from the water is a life-changing experience. Arrive by 6am to beat the crowds and catch the golden light on the peaks.

activities.name: Lake Louise & the Fairmont Chateau
activities.description: Drive 15 minutes from Moraine Lake to the equally stunning Lake Louise. The emerald-green water backed by Victoria Glacier and framed by the Fairmont Chateau is pure grandeur. Hike the Lake Agnes Tea House trail for a rustic alpine experience — 3.4km each way, ending at a lakeside tea house in the mountains.

activities.name: Icefields Parkway — Crowfoot Glacier & Bow Lake
activities.description: Begin the legendary Icefields Parkway drive (Highway 93 North) — consistently rated one of the world's most beautiful roads. Stop at Crowfoot Glacier viewpoint and linger at Bow Lake, the headwaters of the Bow River, where a short walk leads to panoramic glacier views. Pull over at Bow Summit — the highest point on the Icefields Parkway — and hike 1.5km to the Peyto Lake lookout. The glacial-blue lake in the shape of a howling wolf head is one of the most photographed views in Canada.

activities.name: Return to Banff & Banff Hot Springs
activities.description: Head back south toward Banff for the evening. Soak your hiker's legs at the historic Banff Upper Hot Springs — natural mineral hot springs at 1,583m elevation, with views of Sulphur Mountain.

days.title: The Icefields Parkway — Glaciers & Jasper
days.description: Drive the full Icefields Parkway from Banff to Jasper — 232km of the most dramatic mountain scenery on the continent. Stand on the Columbia Icefield, one of the largest non-polar icefields in the world, and end the day in the laid-back mountain town of Jasper.

activities.name: North Along the Icefields Parkway
activities.description: Leave Banff early and drive north on Highway 93 — every corner reveals another waterfall, glacier, or mountain wall. Stop at Sunwapta Falls and the famous waterfalls en route.

activities.name: Columbia Icefield & Athabasca Glacier
activities.description: The Columbia Icefield is the centrepiece of the Icefields Parkway — a 325km² mass of ice that feeds rivers flowing to three different oceans. Walk on the Athabasca Glacier itself via a guided tour or on your own from the toe. The Glacier Skywalk (500m glass-floored walkway) hangs over the valley 280m below.

activities.name: Athabasca Falls
activities.description: Continue north to Athabasca Falls — not the tallest, but arguably the most powerful falls in the Rockies. The Athabasca River narrows into a 23m gorge, creating a roar you feel in your chest. A short trail loops around the falls and canyon. Jasper is smaller and more laid-back than Banff — locals love it for exactly that reason. Check into your accommodation and stroll the compact downtown for dinner.

days.neighborhoods: Johnston Canyon · Banff Gondola · Banff Town
days.title: Johnston Canyon, Gondola Sunset & Farewell
days.description: Drive back south from Jasper for your final day, stopping at one of the Rockies' most magical canyon walks. End with a gondola ride to the summit of Sulphur Mountain for a 360° farewell view of the peaks that have stolen your hearts.

activities.name: Johnston Canyon Catwalk
activities.description: Johnston Canyon is the Canadian Rockies at their most dramatic — a series of catwalks bolted to the canyon walls above a rushing turquoise creek lead to two stunning waterfalls. The Lower Falls (1.1km each way) and Upper Falls (2.7km each way) are both unmissable. Arrive early to beat the day-trippers.

activities.name: Banff Gondola to Sulphur Mountain Summit
activities.description: Ride the Banff Gondola to 2,281m for a 360° panorama of six mountain ranges. The boardwalk on the summit ridge leads to the historic Sanson's Peak meteorological station. On a clear July day, the views stretch endlessly in every direction. On your way out, stop at Two Jack Lake — a serene, underrated gem just minutes from Banff town. Mount Rundle reflects perfectly in the still water. A quiet spot to sit together and take in your last Rockies moment before heading back to Calgary.

activities.name: Drive Back to Calgary (90 min)
activities.description: Begin the drive back east to Calgary for your flight. The last stretch on the Trans-Canada is beautiful as the mountains fade into foothills — a perfect final view of the Rockies in your mirrors.
